title: Raga Todi
hook: a morning raga that opens by admitting need

segments.voice: Yesterday, a hymn in Jaitsri: whole at the beginning, whole in the middle, whole at the end. Your line: strength in jaitsri.

The first minutes after waking are strange ones. The armor isn't on yet. Before the to-do list and the phone and the public face, there's a softer person blinking at the ceiling, who might, for a moment, say what they actually need. Tradition calls today's raga a morning raga, and a tender one. And the hymn that opens it sounds like that unguarded minute: no ceremony, no long praise, just an honest sentence about need. Today: Raga Todi.
screen: `THE FIRST MINUTES AFTER WAKING.` → `BEFORE THE ARMOR GOES ON.` → `AN HONEST SENTENCE ABOUT NEED.`

segments.voice: Todi comes after Jaitsri in the Granth's order. Its first hymn is by Guru Ram Das, mahala four. It begins: har bin reh na sakai man mera. In paraphrase: without the Lord, my mind cannot live. No argument, no description of God's greatness, just dependence, the way a child says I need you. That line opens the refrain, the rahao, the part the hymn keeps coming back to, and it goes on, in paraphrase: my beloved, the breath of my life, is the Lord; the Guru has brought me to meet him, and I won't be tossed again on the terrifying ocean of the world. Notice the order. First the need, said plainly. Then the beloved, named as breath, as close as the air going in and out. Then the meeting, and the steadiness that follows. That's what tender means here. Not weak, not sentimental. Tender is how a person sounds when they stop pretending to be self-sufficient. Tradition sets Todi in the morning, and teachers describe raga moods in different ways, so hold the hour lightly. But you can hear why these words would sit well at dawn, before the armor goes on. A tender morning.
screen: `TODI FOLLOWS JAITSRI.` · `WITHOUT THE LORD, MY MIND CANNOT LIVE.` · `THE BELOVED, THE BREATH OF MY LIFE.` · `TENDER: NO LONGER PRETENDING.` · then, large: `TENDER MORNING.`

segments.voice: Let the shoulders drop, unclench the jaw, and rest the hands open, palms up, breathing as if you'd just woken. Then quietly finish this sentence for yourself, without explaining it: without this, I couldn't live. A person, a faith, the breath itself; if you pray, the answer can be Waheguru.
Raga Todi. The short section after Jaitsri, a morning raga in tradition, which opens with Guru Ram Das saying: without the Lord, my mind cannot live. Today's word.
Your line: tender morning. A morning that starts by telling the truth about what it can't live without. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Shabads from the Todi section of the Guru Granth Sahib are sung in Raga Todi in kirtan, including in morning programs at some gurdwaras, following the tradition that links Todi with the morning.
